sexually_explicit.findings: A starred Kirkus Reviews notice for this memoir identifies childhood sexual abuse and, separately, a consensual sexual encounter as content the book depicts. South Carolina's State Board of Education cited sexual content as grounds for its Feb. 2025 statewide removal order — regional press reported the board's action as following 'sex complaints.' Multiple district-level reconsideration proceedings centered on this same content with different outcomes: Ankeny, Iowa's full-committee review recommended retention (finding the flagged material under 5% of the total text and directing reviewers to judge the work as a whole rather than isolated passages), while in Flagler County, FL, the superintendent ordered removal from media centers even after a district committee had unanimously found the book 'appropriate for use.' This pass could not retrieve a verbatim quoted excerpt of the scene itself — the RED verdict rests on the professional review's explicit content description plus corroborated state/district records, not a fetched primary-text quote.

synopsis: This title carries the heaviest known-list footprint of any book in this run: it is the current #1 title on the ALA's national most-challenged list (2024, its fourth consecutive year listed), was PEN America's #2 most-banned title of the 2021-22 school year, was removed from every South Carolina public school by state board order in February 2025, and appears on Utah's Alpine School District ban list under the state's sensitive-material tracking, with additional reported removals in Florida. On content, a starred Kirkus review and South Carolina's own removal action — reported by regional press as following 'sex complaints' — both point to specific sexual content: a non-consensual sexual encounter with an older family member and a separately depicted consensual encounter, corroborated by multiple district-level reconsideration proceedings (Iowa, Florida) that centered on the same material, though this pass could not retrieve a verbatim quoted passage. Reviewers frame the book's overall theme as Black queer identity and anti-racism/anti-homophobia, not as thematically prurient, so the prurient-theme lens found no evidence; the on-page-explicit-scenes lens did find evidence. No admissible source in this pass supported extreme violence, sustained nudity, indecent content beyond the sexual-content finding above, patently vulgar content, or prohibited website referrals; a general 'profanity' justification appears in press coverage of the challenges but without documented specific instances. Net: a heavy known-list presence paired with genuine, multiply corroborated content evidence — exactly the case where a bare list link would tell a librarian nothing useful.
